newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian amputee held after grenade kills Filipino.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian amputee held after grenade kills Filipino.

text.p: A trainee priest from the Philippines was killed when a grenade exploded as he tried to restrain a physically handicapped Cambodian student, aid workers and a diplomat said on Saturday.

The blast killed Richard Michael Fernando, 26, and injured two students on Thursday at a Jesuit Service Cambodia technical school near Phnom Penh for people disabled by mines and polio, Philippines Consul General Edgardo Manuel told Reuters.

The body of Jesuit priest trainee Fernando, who was in Cambodia performing community service, was sent home on Friday while the student he was trying to disarm was in prison being charged with murder, said the diplomat.

Staff of the Jesuit Service Cambodia said Fernando was killed when he tried to restrain an amputee and former soldier called Sarom, who was brandishing a grenade and threatening to threw it at other students.
The grenade fell behind Fernando, who was killed when shrapnel hit him in the base of the skull and the back.
"If Richie hadn't restrained him, God knows how many people would have been killed, It was a very, very brave thing to do," Jesuit Service Cambodia representative Sister Denise Coghlan told Reuters.
"We're not interested in any sort of revenge," Coghlan said of Sarom, adding: "He's on record as saying, 'Richie, let go, I don't want to kill you'."
